name: Du Jiangtao
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2011-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2009-2026)
forbes_bio: Du Jiangtao is cofounder of Inner Mongolia Junzheng Energy and Beijing Bohui Innovation Technology.
He started the two companies with his wife Hao Hong, a fellow billionaire, more than 20 years ago.
Junzheng Energy manufactures chemical products such as PVC, resin and caustic soda, which is widely used for construction and cleaning products.
Bohui Innovation Technology is a diagnostics company focused primarily on women and children's health.
Du also serves on the education foundation of Beijing Institute of Technology, his alma mater, and on the Zhu Cui Lan Xiang Charity Foundation in Wuhai, a city in Inner Mongolia.

name: Ralph Dommermuth
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Ralph Dommermuth leads United Internet, one of Europe's leading internet specialists serving home users and businesses.
He launched United Internet's predecessor company, 1&1 AG, in 1988 with a borrowed desk and $285,000 saved from working as a computer salesman.
1&1 became the first internet company listed on Germany's stock exchange for high-tech companies, the Neuer Markt, in 1998.
United Internet, of which Dommermuth owns around 50%, has expanded its offerings to include mobile telecommunication services and data centers.
forbes_facts: Dommermuth owns a 5% stake in Borussia Dortmund, a soccer club in the German Bundesliga.
Dommermuth is married to the fashion designer Judith Dommermuth, who sits on Borussia Dortmund's supervisory board.

name: Mahima Datla
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun India (2017-2019)
forbes_bio: Mahima Datla is the managing director of Biological E, a privately held vaccine producer, in which she holds a controlling stake.

The Hyderabad-based company's portfolio includes Corbevax, a Covid-19 vaccine developed in partnership with Texas Children's Hospital Center for Vaccine Development and Baylor College of Medicine in Houston.
Biological E has 10 vaccines pre-qualified by the World Health Organization including those against polio, tetanus and measles. It exports vaccines to more than 130 countries.
Biological E was founded in 1953 by her paternal and maternal grandfathers.
In July 2025 Bioligcal E struck a licensing agreement with China's Jiangsu Recbio Technology to manufacture and commercialize HPV vaccines to combat cancer.
forbes_facts: Datla has a bachelor's degree in business management from London's Webster University. She became managing director in 2013.
In 2022, she won a nearly decade-long battle with her mother over the company's ownership that went up to India's Supreme Court.

name: Michael Hintze
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2010-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Sunday Times Rich List (2020)
forbes_bio: In 1999, Michael Hintze started London-based hedge-fund firm CQS, which was led by the flagship Directional Opportunities fund.
Hintze sold most of CQS' assets to Canadian investment firm Manulife in 2024 and started a new firm called Deltroit with his own capital.
Born in China to Russian parents, Hintze was raised in Australia and served a 3-year stint in the army before making his way to London in the 1980s.
He is a noted supporter of the arts and sciences and was granted Knighthood in 2013 in recognition of his charitable contributions in the U.K.
He maintains a connection to his home country through his MH Premium Farms, which owns a portfolio of agricultural properties in Australia.

name: Roger Wang
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2007-2025)
forbes_bio: Roger Wang is chairman of real estate firm Golden Eagle International, which builds malls and office buildings in eastern China.
The Chinese native grew up in Taiwan and came to the U.S. in 1970 to pursue an M.B.A. from Southeastern Louisiana University.
He got his start through real estate ventures, including condominium development in Los Angeles, before shifting to the market in China in 1992 to start Golden Eagle.
His firm's department store arm, Golden Eagle Retail Group, no longer trades on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange and went private in 2023.
Wang stepped down as chief executive officer of Golden Eagle Retail Group in August 2022 but remains chairman of the parent company, Golden Eagle International Retail Group.
forbes_facts: Wang once sold insurance and managed a drugstore and a furniture company.
His daughter Dorothy Wang is a reality TV star from Rich Kids of Beverly Hills and Famously Single.

name: Hong Feng
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Hurun China (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Hong Feng is a cofounder of Chinese smartphone maker Xiaomi.
Hong no longer holds any position at the company but still derives his net worth from a Xiaomi stake. He was once in charge of its mobile operating system, MIUI.
Hong Feng worked at Siebel, then he joined Google as a senior software engineer who oversaw apps like Google Calendar and Google Map.
He was later a senior product manager at Google China and led the China team to develop a series of local products like Google Music.

name: Harald Tschira
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026)
forbes_bio: Harald Tschira is the son of Klaus Tschira, the software pioneer who cofounded SAP (Systems, Applications, Products) in 1972.
He and his brother Udo inherited their dad's stake in SAP when he died in 2015. Klaus retired from the company in 1998 and left its board in 2007.
His sons carry on the activities of the Klaus Tschira Foundation, which promotes learning in natural sciences, mathematics and computer science.
The foundation, one of Germany's largest philanthropies, has awarded more than $740 million in cash grants and in-kind donations.

name: Stanley Motta
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2024); Hurun Global (2026); Wikidata (2019)
forbes_bio: Stanley Motta is a Panamanian investor with interests in aviation, banking, property, insurance, and the duty-free retail.
His holdings include Copa Airlines, Banco General, ASSA Compañía de Seguros, MKH Capital Partners and Motta Internacional.
Motta interests in Central America include high end real estate and the Panama Canal shipping terminal at Colon, as well as Costa Rica's largest pineapple plantation.
His philanthropic interests include the Nature Conservancy and his alma mater, Tulane University.
